name: optimize_php_allowlist_in_array_loop
description: AllowlistFilter::filter calls in_array() per item against the whole allowlist (O(n*m)) -> array_flip() the allowlist once and use isset() (O(n+m)); calibrated in-container at n=m=100000, naive ~2.7s vs 1200ms budget
prompts: AllowlistFilter::filter in src/AllowlistFilter.php keeps only the items whose 'id' is present in $allowedIds, preserving item order. It checks membership with `in_array($item['id'], $allowedIds, true)` inside the loop, which linearly rescans the whole allowlist for every item - O(n*m) total, far too slow when both the item list and the allowlist are large. Rewrite it to run in O(n+m): build an id -> present lookup from $allowedIds ONCE (e.g. via array_flip), then do an O(1) isset() check per item. Keep the exact same output: only allowed items, in their original relative order, duplicates kept.

setup_files.src/AllowlistFilter.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class AllowlistFilter
{
    // Keep only the items whose id is present in $allowedIds, order preserved.
    // BUG: in_array() does a linear scan of $allowedIds for EVERY item, so
    // filtering n items against an allowlist of size m is O(n*m).
    public function filter(array $items, array $allowedIds): array
    {
        $out = [];
        foreach ($items as $item) {
            if (in_array($item['id'], $allowedIds, true)) {
                $out[] = $item;
            }
        }
        return $out;
    }
}

test_setup_files.tests/AllowlistFilterTest.php:
<?php
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

require_once __DIR__ . '/../src/AllowlistFilter.php';

final class AllowlistFilterTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testKeepsOnlyAllowedInOrder(): void
    {
        $f = new \App\AllowlistFilter();
        $items = [['id' => 1], ['id' => 2], ['id' => 3], ['id' => 4]];
        $this->assertSame(
            [['id' => 2], ['id' => 4]],
            $f->filter($items, [2, 4])
        );
    }

    public function testEmptyAllowlist(): void
    {
        $f = new \App\AllowlistFilter();
        $this->assertSame([], $f->filter([['id' => 1]], []));
    }

    public function testPreservesDuplicateItems(): void
    {
        $f = new \App\AllowlistFilter();
        $items = [['id' => 1], ['id' => 1], ['id' => 2]];
        $this->assertSame(
            [['id' => 1], ['id' => 1]],
            $f->filter($items, [1])
        );
    }

    public function testPerformanceLargeInput(): void
    {
        $n = 100000;
        $m = 100000;
        $items = [];
        for ($i = 0; $i < $n; $i++) {
            $items[] = ['id' => $i];
        }
        $allowedIds = [];
        for ($i = 0; $i < $m; $i += 2) {
            $allowedIds[] = $i;
        }
        $expected = [];
        foreach ($items as $item) {
            if ($item['id'] % 2 === 0) {
                $expected[] = $item;
            }
        }

        $f = new \App\AllowlistFilter();
        $t0 = microtime(true);
        $got = $f->filter($items, $allowedIds);
        $dt = microtime(true) - $t0;

        $this->assertSame($expected, $got);
        $this->assertLessThan(
            1.2,
            $dt,
            sprintf('filter took %.3fs for %d items / %d allowlist entries; expected O(n+m), not in_array() per item', $dt, $n, $m)
        );
    }
}

reference_solution.src/AllowlistFilter.php:
<?php
namespace App;

class AllowlistFilter
{
    // array_flip() builds an id -> index lookup ONCE (O(m)); isset() is then
    // O(1) per item, giving O(n + m) total instead of O(n*m).
    public function filter(array $items, array $allowedIds): array
    {
        $allowed = array_flip($allowedIds);
        $out = [];
        foreach ($items as $item) {
            if (isset($allowed[$item['id']])) {
                $out[] = $item;
            }
        }
        return $out;
    }
}

<?php
namespace App;

class AllowlistFilter
{
    public function filter(array $items, array $allowedIds): array
    {
        $flippedItems = array_flip(array_column($items, 'id'));
        $out = [];
        foreach ($allowedIds as $id) {
            if (isset($flippedItems[$id])) {
                $out[] = ['id' => $id];
            }
        }
        return $out;
    }
}
